# 08-fresco — sources

Back-test entry `08-fresco.yaml`: Fresco, the AI scribe for construction superintendents (YC Fall 2024).
Written 2026-10-22 from public material only. Quotes are verbatim from the page named; "Author's choice" marks the
smallest plausible choice made where the public material is silent.

Main sources:
- [HN] Launch HN: Fresco (YC F24), 2024-11-21 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42204939
- [LYC] Launch YC: Fresco, the scribe for construction, 2024-10-23 — https://www.ycombinator.com/launches/M73-fresco-the-scribe-for-construction
- [YCP] YC company page — https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/fresco (now "AI-powered takeoff and estimating for Division 8 construction")
- [KOE] A contractor's daily-log expectations on Procore's support site — https://support.procore.com/tc/Koester/Site_Map/Koester_Expectations_-_Daily_Logs
- [SWI] Swiftask, Procore daily reports page (vendor) — https://swiftask.ai/ai-integration/procore/intelligent-daily-reports
- [BLS] BLS Occupational Outlook, construction managers — https://www.bls.gov/ooh/management/construction-managers.htm
- [OPU] Launch HN: Opusense (field reports for site inspectors), 2025-05-20 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44042791

## The eight founder-emulation items

1. **Who.** Construction superintendents on commercial jobs.
   [HN] "Superintendents are the busiest and most expensive people on construction sites."
   [LYC] "That’s the reality for 210k+ construction superintendents (or supervisors, foremen, PMs, etc.) across the USA."
   → `roles[superintendent]`, `context.actor`, `actor_plural`. Author's choice: "on commercial jobs" (the founders ask
   for introductions to commercial general contractors in [LYC]).

2. **What (the job).** Keep the record of the day's work, for liability and disputes.
   [HN] "30-200 photos per day to document site progress (mostly for liability reasons, or in case of a dispute with the
   owner over delays and deliverables)"; photos used to create "daily logs", "structured documents that account for the
   work done on site on any given day". [KOE] the log is "a critical piece of documentation in the arbitration of a
   dispute". → `statements.problem`, `context.job`, `interpretations.problem`.

3. **When / where.** At the end of the day, after the site walks, in the trailer.
   [HN] "At the end of the day, they'll spend a few hours uploading those photos into OneDrive, or project management
   software like Procore or ACC." [YCP] "We were curious what superintendents were doing for hours in their trailers at
   the end of the day." [LYC] "supes are spending up to 3 hours a day creating documents". → `context.circumstance`, `occasion: daily log`.
   Author's choice: the recall window {5, WORKING_DAYS} and Frequency 4 to 5 working days out of 5 (the posts say "per
   day"; a five-day site week is assumed). Prevalence `p_80_100` ("Nearly all") follows from the same "per day".

4. **Which people (the comparable group).** Superintendents at US general contractors whose jobs run on Procore or ACC.
   [LYC] "210k+ construction superintendents ... across the USA"; "Project management tools like Procore and ACC have
   dramatically increased documentation requirements". [YCP] "driving to Napa, South Bay, and around SF". → `context.segment`,
   `market: US`.

5. **Who pays.** The general contractor, per site.
   [HN] "we charge per site per month, which includes unlimited users on any given construction project".
   → `persona.decision_maker: {role: contractor}`, the BUYER role. Author's choice: the decider is the contractor's
   "operations lead" and the role to test is "The CFO" (a second role, "The project executive", listed); Purchase
   friction's three steps ("A trial on one live job" tested, a Procore check, a security review) and Commitment's step
   "start a paid pilot on one site" are the author's. Public material names no buyer title; [LYC] asks for
   introductions to general contractors by firm, not by role.

6. **Mechanism.** Narrated short videos turned into notes, texted to the crew, pushed to Procore/ACC.
   [HN] "Supers simply take short videos with voiceover, or upload photos, and Fresco does the rest, creating notes with
   transcription, photos, assignees, and due dates. Supers can easily text their crew action items, and receive texts
   back". "We also route this to whatever project management software they're using with a single click."
   [LYC] the narrated example "The beam in the southwest corner of room 134 is corroded and needs replacement by Alex.";
   "Supes who use Fresco complete their notes, on average, 90% faster."
   → `statements.solution`, `solution_mechanism`, Compatibility and Adoption friction items. Relative advantage's two
   benefits are from [HN] ("during their site walks, not after") and [LYC] ("90% faster"); their wording is the author's.

7. **Price.** About $1k per site per month, less with multi-site or multi-month terms.
   [HN] "The typical price is $1k/month, but we offer discounts for multi-month or multi-site commitments."
   → `commercial.price` {800, 1000, month}. Author's choice: the low end of $800 stands for the stated discounts.
   Existing sacrifice: 30 to 60 hours a month per site at an hourly rate of 55 — from [LYC] "up to 3 hours a day" and
   [HN] "a few hours uploading", taken as 1.5 to 3 hours on about twenty working days (author's arithmetic). The rate is
   [BLS] "$55.28 per hour" (median, construction managers, May 2025), the author's stand-in: no superintendent wage is
   in the public material. Ability to pay is derived by code (24% to 61%).

8. **Occasions.** The narrated beam; a school refit report; the uploads and logs at the end of the day.
   [LYC] on a school refit walkthrough: "Normally, creating the final report takes 2+ hours."
   [HN] "few supers have time to do this thoroughly, so these photos aren't very searchable." No named customer quote
   exists in public; the occasions below are scripted from these and from practitioner comments.

## Open
- The verdict was scripted to be plausible and not obviously "build": the problem holds on how often but people
  disagree on whether the log is one of their two worst difficulties; the solution splits on the benefit and on
  talking over videos on site; the price fails (two of eight at the founder's band or above) while the cost it would
  replace is above the price. This is the author's reading of the thread's sceptics, not a measured result.
- No public account names a buyer title at a general contractor; the decider, the tested role "The CFO", the purchase
  steps and the Commitment step are the author's.
- hourly_rate 55 is a proxy (construction managers, not superintendents).
- Existing sacrifice picks use `period: quarter` (the corpus's convention), although the registry's recall period for a
  monthly cost reads "last month"; the values are the monthly figures times three.
- The window {5, WORKING_DAYS} is the author's; the public posts say "per day".

screens.why1: After listing what supers must do to start, asking which effort is most likely to stop them is the obvious next step before Keel picks the one adoption question to test.
screens.why2: Both options are in my own words; walks, short videos and talking over them are how I described it, and the intro says plainly that I pick one.
screens.why3: I know my supers and I know the real sticking point is whether they will narrate videos on a loud site in front of the crew, so I can answer this from what I see.
screens.why4: The two efforts are distinct and in my words, but the list leaves out pushing the notes to Procore or ACC and texting the crew, so it is thin even though my true pick is there.
screens.why5: The belief and the test read exactly as I typed it, take short videos and talk over them on walks, with nothing reworded.

screens.why1: Right before the study goes out is the obvious place to decide whether to ask strangers for a pilot, and I want supers who'd try it on a live job.
screens.why2: Short question, and the hint spells out exactly what the respondent will see and where I'll find the yeses.
screens.why3: Whether I want pilot leads is my own call as the founder, nothing to guess.
screens.why4: Yes or No covers it, the two are distinct, and nothing is missing.
screens.why5: The line respondents get, "Would you try this for real?", fits a super, but a pilot for me is a paid pilot on one site that the contractor signs off on, and the screen doesn't say whether this asks the super or the buyer.
screens.instead: Offer a pilot? People who say yes get a line at the end: "Would you try this on one of your jobs? Leave your email." (Yes, ask them / No pilot)

screens.why1: Just before the link goes out to supers, it makes sense to pick who asks them, and it comes after the pilot offer, as the last setup step.
screens.why2: Plain enough, but the hint calls the choice a voice while the interviewer is on video and my pick was to lock 'the face', so I'd read it twice to see whether I'm choosing a voice, a face or both.
screens.why3: As the founder I can judge which interviewer a super in a trailer at the end of the day would sit through, and the hint answers my real worries about cost (same 400 credits either way) and delivery (by text).
screens.why4: Two named interviewers, each with a 5-second sample, the default marked, and a flat price either way: complete and distinct for this choice.
screens.why5: It keeps my wording, 'construction superintendents', and nothing of Fresco or the contractor roles leaks into it.
screens.instead: Who should ask construction superintendents your questions on video? (Daphne, picked for you / Saskia; tap to hear each for 5 s; same 400 credits either way, sent by text)

screens.why1: Choosing how my supers will answer belongs here, right after picking who asks the questions and just before sending, and it isn't asked anywhere else in the flow.
screens.why2: Most of it reads cleanly, but 'Still recording · ready in a few minutes' made me pause: is Daphne's video still being made, or is something recording me?
screens.why3: I know my supers fill things in on a phone in a loud trailer or on site, so I can judge talking versus tapping from what I see every day.
screens.why4: Voice, text and their own pick are the three real choices; they are distinct, and the loud-room accuracy line is exactly what I'd weigh for a jobsite.
screens.why5: It calls them superintendents and leaks nothing of Fresco's product or the buyer roles; my pick, Read and tap, stands as I chose it.
screens.instead: Same three options, with Daphne's status reading 'Her video is still being made, ready in a few minutes'.

screens.why1: Right after choosing how superintendents answer, the obvious last step is who gets the links, and as the founder I have supers I've met on site walks in Napa and the South Bay to send to.
screens.why2: Plain founder's words: by name, from a search list, or one open link posted where people already are; 'Contacts page' is Keel's own page and is explained in line.
screens.why3: I know whether I'm sending to supers I've met on site visits or posting in a group, so I can answer this from my own situation.
screens.why4: The three routes are distinct and clear, but there is no way to say 'a mix' (a few supers by name plus an open link in a superintendents' group), which is how I'd actually recruit.
screens.why5: Nothing of my idea is reworded here, and the screen leaks nothing about Fresco or the buyer roles to respondents.
screens.instead: Who gets a link? (pick any) — People I know by name, each their own link / People I found with Keel, from a list on the Contacts page / A group, with one open link I post where they already are

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits under the title, and each card gives its deciding number beside it: '4 answered · 5 needed to call it'.
screens.why_b2: The tally '3 too few · 7 people answered' takes a second look: '3' counts cards, not people, and the headline 7 doesn't square with the 4 answered on every card.
screens.why_b3: Compatibility, Relative advantage and Adoption friction carry exactly the belief lines I checked on the way in, word for word.
screens.why_b4: '5 needed to call it' implies I need one more answer per card, but the screen never says so, nor who to send it to (more supers, not the ops leads).
screens.why_b5: It claims nothing beyond the data and says the n is too low, but the headline '7 people answered' next to '4 answered' per card leaves unexplained who the other 3 are and why they don't count.
screens.instead: Too few to call on all three cards: 4 of the 7 who answered were superintendents asked these questions (the other 3 were buyers, not asked); one more superintendent answer per card would let Keel call it, so send the study to a few more supes.

screens.why_b1: "Too few to call" sits beside "5 needed", but the header says "4 answered" while the count line says "5 answered · 4 counted", so I have to work out which number decides it.
screens.why_b2: The chart counts 4 supers with the bar at 3 of 4, which is plain, but the strip's fifth ghost cell and the clashing answered/counted figures need a second look.
screens.why_b3: Compatibility and "they could talk over the noise on site" are my words as I checked them.
screens.why_b4: "Ray's no is the one to ask about" points somewhere, but it doesn't say to get one more super counted or what to ask Ray, and it gives no step for whether talking over the noise works.
screens.why_b5: It doesn't call the result, which is right, but the question asked whether the log "fitted the way things were set up", not whether a super could talk over site noise, and the header says 4 answered when 5 did.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 3 of the 4 supers counted said it would have fitted their last log (Luis's guess not counted), but nobody was asked about talking over site noise, so ask Ray what didn't fit and ask one more super whether they could narrate on a loud deck.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits right beside its deciding number, 4 counted against 5 needed, so I know why nothing was called.
screens.why_b2: Three 'a lot better' and one 'no difference' over four is plain, but 'your bar · 3 of 4' with the marker at 3 takes a second look, because my bar was 'no more than 1 in 3 against', not '3 for'.
screens.why_b3: Relative advantage and 'their last daily log would have gone better with it: hours back at the end of the day' are the words I checked on the way in.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' doesn't tell me the lean is my way, or that one more counted superintendent would settle it.
screens.why_b5: The low n is said and the lean is not called a result, but the header says '4 answered' while the count line says '5 answered · 4 counted', which blurs who answered with who counted.
screens.instead: Leaning your way but too few to call: 3 of 4 counted supers say a lot better and 1 (Denise, whose log is done at the gate) says no difference; Luis's answer was a guess, so get one more clear answer to settle it.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits right beside the deciding number, 4 counted against 5 needed, though the header's '4 answered' clashes with the count line's '5 answered · 4 counted'.
screens.why_b2: I can see the chart counts the four answer choices over 4 people, but 'your bar · 3 of 4' next to 3 for and 1 against looks like I passed, so I had to look twice to see why it isn't called.
screens.why_b3: The belief 'Most would take short videos and talk over them on walks' is the line I checked, word for word.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' tells me to wait but not what to do: find one more superintendent who describes a real walk, or chase the two 'if it was clearly worth it' answers.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible, the small group is called 'a lean, not a call', the two conditional yeses are flagged as conditional, and Luis's guess is set aside rather than counted.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 4 of 5 needed counted (Luis's answer was a guess). Of the 3 who'd do it, 2 said only if clearly worth it, so get one more real answer and find out what 'worth it' means to them before leaning on video-and-voiceover.

screens.why_b1: Each box opens on "Too few to call" with "4 answered · 5 needed to call it" beside it, so the verdict and the number behind it agree and sit together.
screens.why_b3: The names Compatibility and Relative advantage and both belief lines are word for word what I checked, the noise on site and hours back at the end of the day.
screens.why_b4: "5 needed to call it" implies I need one more answer, but the screen never says that or what two whys pointing away from the log mean for Fresco.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible on every box, the low count is named as too few to call, and each group is shown as one person, so nothing claims more than the answers carry.
screens.why_b6: Ray and Denise both say the schedule and no-show subs eat the day and the log can wait or is already done on a tablet, which tells me the log may not be the pain I typed in.
screens.instead: One more answer calls each line; so far both whys say the schedule and no-show subs eat the day, not the log, so test whether Fresco's texting the crew matters more than the log.

screens.why1: As the very first screen, checking whether my jobs run on Procore or ACC is the obvious gate before asking about my daily logs.
screens.why2: Procore and ACC are the platforms every super at a GC knows by name, and "any job you run now" is how I'd say it.
screens.why3: I know exactly what my current job runs on because I'm in it every day doing the daily log.
screens.why4: Yes or No covers it cleanly for a gate, and the screener rightly carries no escape.
screens.why5: It asks only about the platform my job runs on, with nothing of the founder's product or terms leaking through.
screens.why6: Heard aloud it's short, but "ACC" is an abbreviation that only says well to someone who already knows it, and "I'll read 2 options" for a plain yes-or-no is clunky where "Yes or no" would do.
screens.instead: Is any job you run now on Procore or Autodesk Construction Cloud? Yes or no.

screens.why1: Right after asking whether my job runs on Procore, asking whether I did the daily log myself this week makes sense as the gate before the story.
screens.why2: "Type up by hand" is muddled: I type the log into Procore every day, so I can't tell whether "by hand" means typing it myself or writing it on paper.
screens.why3: I do the daily log every working day, so I know whether I did it in the last five.
screens.why4: Yes and No cover it, but a gate shouldn't carry escapes, and here there are two: "I'd rather not say" and a sentence-long "I can't recall one particular daily log" that makes no sense when I do one every day.
screens.why5: "By hand" hints that the alternative is something that writes the log for me, which drifts from simply asking whether I did the log myself.
screens.why6: Short, one question, "Yes or no" said cleanly; the chips aren't read aloud.
screens.instead: In the last 5 working days, did you write up the daily log yourself? Yes / No

screens.why1: Right after asking whether I typed up the daily log by hand, showing me an idea that turns my site walk into notes and a Procore or ACC entry is the obvious next step.
screens.why2: Site walk, crew, action items, assignees and Procore or ACC are all words I use every day, so I get it on first read.
screens.why3: I walk the site with my phone every day, taking photos and notes that end up in Procore, so I can picture this on my own job.
screens.why4: It's a card to read, with no options.
screens.why5: The study opened on keeping the daily log, but the card leans toward punch-style action items with assignees, due dates and crew texts, so the daily-log record drifts a little; the opening also calls it 'site walk notes with photos' instead of saying what it is, an AI scribe for site walks.
screens.why6: Heard aloud, the last sentence re-lists the videos, notes, texts and Procore entry I just heard, so it runs long and repeats itself instead of pointing back.
screens.instead: Imagine Fresco, an AI scribe for site walks. During the walk you take short videos and talk over them; it turns them into the day's log with photos, texts the crew their items, and sends it to Procore or ACC in one click. The people building it believe it would save you the hours of typing up the log after the walk.

screens.why1: Right after the idea card, asking whether it would have worked with how my last daily log got done is the obvious next thing to ask me.
screens.why2: "Fitted the way things were set up for you" is fuzzy: I'd have to read it twice to work out whether it means our Procore setup, the company's log template, or how my super day runs, and "it" means Fresco only if I remember the card.
screens.why3: I know how my last log went into Procore, but I'd be guessing what "set up" covers and how notes from a walk would land there.
screens.why4: "Most of the time" and "only sometimes" are odd answers about one daily log, which either fit or didn't, so the scale reads like it was built for a habit and not a single day.
screens.why5: Nothing leaks, but the question has lost what it should fit (Procore or ACC, our log format), so it has drifted into a general "would it fit".
screens.why6: Short, one question, and four short options plus one escape that I can hold after hearing them once.
screens.instead: Think of your last daily log. Could Fresco's notes and photos have gone straight into Procore? Yes; yes, with some steps; or no. Or say you can't tell.

screens.why1: Right after asking if it would fit how my jobs are set up, asking whether it would have actually helped with my last daily log is the obvious next thing.
screens.why2: I get it on first hearing, but 'go better' leaves me guessing whether you mean faster, less time uploading photos to Procore, or a log that holds up in a delay dispute.
screens.why3: I wrote my last daily log, so I can judge whether something that took my site walk notes and photos would have helped.
screens.why4: A lot better, a little better, no difference, worse covers it cleanly, and 'I can't tell' fits if I can't picture the tool on my job.
screens.why5: It's about the daily log and site walk notes with photos, which is my world, and nothing in it sounds like a sales pitch or someone else's job title.
screens.why6: One short question, four short options I can hold, one escape at the end; easy to answer by ear.
screens.instead: Would Fresco have got your last daily log done quicker, or not? A lot quicker; a little quicker; no difference; slower; or I can't tell.

screens.why1: Right after the card and the fit and better-or-not questions, asking whether I'd actually shoot video and talk over it on my walks is the obvious last thing to ask.
screens.why2: Short videos, talking over them, walks: that's how I'd say it myself, and I get it on one hearing.
screens.why3: I walk the job every day with my phone out, so I know whether I'd narrate clips with the noise, the gloves and the crew stopping me every ten feet.
screens.why4: Yes, yes if it's worth it, probably not, and no cover where I'd land without overlapping, and 'I can't tell' fits if I haven't tried it.
screens.why5: The card right above says site walk notes with photos, but the question says short videos, so I'm left wondering which one it actually is.
screens.why6: One short question, four short options I can hold, and the escape said last; it says well.
screens.instead: Imagine Fresco, site walk notes from short videos. To use it, you'd take short videos and talk over them on your walks. Would you do that, or not? Yes · Yes, if it was clearly worth it · Probably not · No · I can't tell
